  • The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club opting to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

It has been revealed that the departure is understood to be amicable and won’t take immediate effect. Stewart could continue attending matches before formally leaving, following discussions with co-owner Behdad Eghbali over the club’s evolving sporting structure.

The story was first reported by Matt Law of The Telegraph and Nizaar Kinsella of BBC Sport, with Ben Jacobs subsequently providing further details about how Chelsea intend to operate.

Stewart arrived from Monaco in October 2022 as technical director before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley in February 2023.

Chelsea’s day-to-day sporting leadership will now be shared between Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields, each with defined responsibilities.

Recent findings suggest that winstanley will continue overseeing transfer negotiations, player contracts and several departments at Cobham, including medical and performance operations. Shields’ work centres on the academy and player pathways, while Jewell has wider responsibilities across the BlueCo operation, including Strasbourg.

According to Jacobs, discussions about restructuring began in April and accelerated following the appointment of Xabi Alonso as head coach.

Stewart had overseen investment in Chelsea’s data analysis operation, although Jewell and Shields have increasingly taken responsibility for using that information in recruitment and talent identification.

Dave Fallows will remain involved in an advisory capacity, rather than taking on a fixed day-to-day portfolio.

The changes are being described as a natural evolution of Chelsea’s sporting model. There is no suggestion that Stewart’s departure followed a breakdown in relations, and the club are not currently planning to recruit a replacement.

There will be no live UK television coverage of Chelsea’s return to Premier League action against Bournemouth on Saturday afternoon.

Xabi Alonso’s side host the Cherries at Stamford Bridge in a traditional 3pm kick-off, with the fixture falling within the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

That means supporters unable to attend will need to follow the match through other channels, rather than watching it live on Sky Sports or TNT Sports.

Although the game will not be televised live in the UK, supporters can follow developments through the official Chelsea website and the Premier League website.

The Saturday 3pm blackout prevents live domestic television broadcasts during the restricted period, although overseas coverage may be available through broadcasters holding the relevant rights.

Highlights will be available after the match through the usual broadcast and digital channels, subject to their respective release schedules.

Chelsea will then turn their attention to a trip to Everton on Saturday, 17 October, with that fixture scheduled for a 12.30pm kick-off at Hill Dickinson Stadium.

For Alonso, the Bournemouth match provides the immediate opportunity to resume Chelsea’s domestic campaign following the international break.

That figure has not been established as a firm asking price, however, and Brus reports that industry sources expect the eventual cost to be lower. Chelsea’s previous investment of approximately £51m in Estevao is regarded as a possible benchmark.

Manchester City’s ownership group have also made contact regarding Conceicao, while Arsenal, Manchester United, Barcelona, Real Madrid, Bayern Munich and Paris Saint-Germain are among the clubs reported to have watched him.

Chelsea’s existing relationship with Palmeiras could help their efforts, although the level of competition means there is no guarantee that their early interest will lead to a deal.

The player’s age is another consideration. Conceicao cannot complete an international transfer to England until he turns 18, leaving interested clubs facing a potentially lengthy wait before he can join their squads.

Chelsea have already demonstrated their willingness to agree deals for young players well before they are eligible to arrive, with Estevao providing a particularly relevant example.

Recent findings suggest that no formal bid or agreement has been reported for Conceicao. Nevertheless, the latest claims suggest Chelsea are prepared to explore another long-term investment in Brazilian talent rather than wait until the player becomes available for an immediate move.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 12:49, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 16:37.

Life without Vitor Matos begins for Swansea City on Saturday afternoon, when fellow promotion hopefuls West Bromwich Albion visit Swansea.com Stadium for a Championship battle.

The Swans have lost their Portuguese mastermind to Ligue 1 following a poor run of form prior to the international break, whereas the Baggies come into this South Wales clash full of confidence.

After being linked to vacant roles at Crystal Palace and Sporting Lisbon over the past month, Swansea head coach Matos has been poached by Ligue 1 outfit Strasbourg, leaving the Welsh side without a permanent manager this weekend.

The 38-year-old's departure comes after an overall impressive start to the season for the Swans, however, they have lost four of their past five second-tier matches, falling to defeat by Birmingham City on November 7.

Collecting just three points from Matos's final five games at the helm, Swansea have slid down to sixth place in the Championship standings after 15 matches, still just three points behind the league leaders.

Alarmingly, a once-watertight defence has conceded 11 goals across its last five contests in the second tier, although the Swans were excellent in their most recent home match, smashing Blackburn Rovers by a 4-0 scoreline.

Former Swansea defender Ashley Williams is expected to join Leon Britton and Kris O'Leary in an interim coaching group on Saturday afternoon, when the hosts will look to extend their unbeaten home run against West Brom to eight matches.

Concerns regarding a potential relegation to League One in the spring feel a million miles away from The Hawthorns right now, with West Brom targeting an unlikely promotion push at the top of the Championship.

Since losing to pacesetters Birmingham on October 10, the Baggies have strung together an impressive six-match unbeaten run (W4 D2) in the second tier, enjoying a standout home success last time out.

James Morrison's troops took full advantage of a wounded Lions pack in the Black Country on November 7, when Isaac Price, Jayson Molumby and Norway international Felix Horn Myhre all netted in the demolition of Millwall.

Yet to be defeated by a club below them in the league standings so far this season, West Brom are right now occupying fifth position, just a single point behind Blues, Middlesbrough and Stoke City at the summit of the division.

The Albion were simply awful on the road during the opening months of 2026 but have improved massively under the stewardship of Morrison, who has masterminded wins at Wrexham (2-1) and West Ham United (3-1) over the past few weeks.

Swansea were unsuccessful in their appeal of Marko Stamenic's red card at Birmingham prior to the international pause.

As a result, the New Zealander is sidelined for the next three matches, including the South Wales derby against Cardiff City on November 29.

Goncalo Franco and Stephen Welsh are both doubts for this weekend's game due to muscular problems.

West Brom suffered a major fitness blow during the two-week break, with influential midfielder Ousmane Diakite picking up a calf injury whilst on duty for Mali.

The much-improved 26-year-old faces at least eight weeks on the sidelines, joining fellow midfielder Toby Collyer in the medical room.

The Baggies are also short on options in defence, with Noah Galves (knee) out of action, but captain George Campbell is available for selection.

Rocked by the sudden departure of Matos, Swansea will be chasing home comforts in South Wales this weekend.

Even without Diakite, West Brom should be good enough for a share of the spoils with the managerless Swans.

£380m = zero points: Major-spending Spurs humbled by Newcastle

⏱️ ~24 mins left to finish

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, these remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see.
  • Industry observers note that not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net.
  • This meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, these remain the earliest of early days but the blunt facts are there for all to see. Tottenham Hotspur, the club that has spent around £380m this summer in search of instant improvements, have played twice and lost twice in the Premier League. After making eight upcoming signings, they have so far scored zero goals and won zero points.

Industry observers note that not since 1974 has a Spurs team lost the first two games of a league campaign without finding the net. The summer enthusiasm in this corner of north London is therefore already drifting away, to the sound of an alarmingly familiar soundtrack: boos from the home supporters at the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium.

This meeting with Newcastle United was, in the minds of those Spurs fans, meant to be a clash between a team remade by the transfer market and a team broken by it. Yet it was Newcastle, still adjusting to the loss of three key players this summer, who looked the more unified group and more organised team.

It proved to be a truly glorious evening for the visiting supporters, who not only delighted in their team’s victory but also in the struggles of Sandro Tonali. The £100m Italian, who swapped Newcastle for Spurs a few weeks ago, never came close to offering the sort of class one would expect for such a fee. That price tag is not his fault but it is his burden, and in time he will need to shoulder it more impressively than he did here.

Roberto De Zerbi, the Spurs head coach, can rightly say that it will take time for his new group to develop the cohesion he needs. The worrying reality for Spurs, though, is that his opposite number had far less time to work with his players and far less money to reshape his squad. Matthias Jaissle appears to be a man with a defined blueprint, and an ability to convey it. Newcastle improved considerably after half-time, which spoke volumes of Jaissle’s work. “He is the best signing of Newcastle so far,” mentioned Yoane Wissa of his new coach.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc.

According to recent reports, for Spurs, so much of it would have felt painfully similar to last season, when they won only three home games in the Premier League. They played some pretty football in bursts, but not at the crucial points of the game. The second half, especially, was pockmarked with moments of despair. There was Mathys Tel’s free-kick that almost flew into Islington, for example, and Mateus Fernandes falling over when running onto a pass in the penalty area.

In a recent development, de Zerbi stated he was sorry for the fans and for the club, and suggested his team is not properly prepared for this campaign. “Maybe we are not ready yet,” he said. “For many, many reasons we are not ready yet.”.

"I have no panic, I know very well where I'm going" Roberto De Zerbi apologises to Spurs fans after the defeat to Newcastle 🔊 pic.twitter.com/83DntjG5ZH.

Newcastle’s two goals, much like Brentford’s three last weekend, exposed the enduring frailties in the Spurs defence. Anthony Elanga’s opener stemmed from a long pass over the top of the home side’s high line, while Wissa’s acrobatic effort came from a corner kick that Spurs could not handle. Neither strike, it would be safe to say, was the result of world-class attacking play.

Anthony Elanga finishes brilliantly and celebrates just as Thierry Henry did against Spurs 💥 pic.twitter.com/l6qndlMrKm.

What a GOAL from Yoane Wissa?! 🫨 pic.twitter.com/mjuHpaa4YY.

“After the first goal we lost confidence,” said De Zerbi. “The reaction was not good enough, not what I want to see on the pitch. The solution is not to put the head down, but to react.”.

To be clear, Spurs were not quite as bad as they had been against Brentford on the opening day. They did create chances here, taking 17 shots and forcing a few terrific saves from Lukas Hornicek, Newcastle’s impressive goalkeeper. But in the key moments they suffered from the same absence of clarity and execution as they did last season. Troublingly, this seemed to affect the newly introduced signings as much as it did the longer-serving players.

Of the five upcoming arrivals who featured for Spurs, Tonali was the least effective. The Italian had been vigorously booed by the away fans before kick-off and the travelling Geordies waited with palpable excitement for his first mistake. Much to their delight, it arrived after only three minutes: an underhit pass, in his own half, which directly led to Micky van de Ven picking up a yellow card. Tonali was outshone by new Newcastle midfielder Nico Gonzalez, who excelled only a few days after completing his move from Manchester City.

"He's got an opportunity to be the main man"Jamie Redknapp praises Nico Gonzalez's performance on his debut 👏 pic.twitter.com/1ga3tsxXHA.

Industry observers note that might it have been different for Spurs if £75m winger Savio had been available? The Brazilian was electrifying on his debut in midweek, when he scored against Charlton Athletic in the League Cup, yet was unavailable here due to a minor injury. It instead fell to another signing from City, Omar Marmoush, to lead the attack. He was busy and floaty but never truly hurt Newcastle.

Sources indicate that there are more changes to come at Spurs before Tuesday’s deadline. De Zerbi revealed after the game that Richarlison, Kevin Danso and Pape Matar Sarr have all asked to leave the club.

Industry observers note that at least the problems facing his players appear clear to De Zerbi. His list of areas to improve was lengthy – he spoke of strengthening the connection between the players, the quality of their play, their work in the defensive phase and the distances between them – but he also insisted he loves them and remains confident in the club’s project. At this rate, though, the fans might not share that confidence for much longer.

Recent findings suggest that the Tottenham boss told BBC Sport: “Disappointed for the result because until the first goal we conceded I think we played better than Newcastle. We lost ball possession in the first half because we didn’t defend in the right way, the distance between the defenders and attackers was too major. We can improve in the defensive phases but today was an unfair result.

According to recent reports, “At the beginning of the second half we had some chance to create the potential chances. We created many chances to score, we have to improve the last decision, because that will make a difference. At the end we are disappointed for the result and our fans. We are working to be a great team. When we become a team I think we can change the story of the last two seasons for Tottenham.

“We are working to be good on the pitch, if you believe in work and training then you have to improve day by day.”.

Industry observers note that speaking to Sky Sports, Newcastle’s head coach said: “It was incredible and I’m really proud. We are really proud as a club, as a coaching staff to see a team on the pitch delivering the match strategy at a high level already, but also seeing players fully committed to what we’re doing. This is a good start and a moment to enjoy.

“We also did well last week against Liverpool, therefore it was a step in the right direction again against a strong opponent with huge signings during the transfer window. This is something we were aware of, but how we handled that challenge was amazing.”.

"He is the best signing for Newcastle"Yoane Wissa praises Matthias Jaissle's impact at the club since becoming head coach 👔 pic.twitter.com/dX8nVknpKc.

"With the fans behind us, no one can stop us" 🖤Yoane Wissa reacts to Newcastle's win at Spurs! pic.twitter.com/itaiVO3Kx1.

After a tumultuous summer, Jaissle has ushered in a new era of hope and positivity at Newcastle, with Wissa and Elanga reborn in attack.

"Oh Jaissle, I can boogie..." 🎶🕺 pic.twitter.com/FmvC2DrLMO.

2 - Anthony Elanga is the first player to score in both of Newcastle United's first two Premier League games of a campaign since Alan Shearer in 2003-04.Footsteps. pic.twitter.com/VZ3hXEbpG7.

It has been revealed that jaissle records his first ever Premier League win, heaping more misery upon Tottenham, who begin the season with two defeats. Excellent second-half finishes from Elanga and Wissa have given the visitors a superb three points in the capital.

Industry observers note that barnes attempts to latch onto a ball in behind, but Kinsky races out to claim. Spurs then almost half-heartedly come forward as Udogie tries to find Marmoush with a powerful cross. Recent findings suggest that fernandes clips a pinpoint cross into Marmoush. The Egyptian shoots via a first-time volley, but his tame attempt is easily gathered by Hornicek.

Van de Ven’s reintegration into Spurs’ defence hasn’t proved helpful. The hosts have been all at sea at the back since the restart. Newcastle indicated little attacking ambition in the first half but have ripped Tottenham apart in the second.

Industry observers note that jaissle makes another double change as both goal-scorers, Elanga and Wissa, are taken off for Murphy and Ramsey. Elanga and Wissa have both produced extremely positive displays to kickstart their seasons under their new head coach.

Spurs have looked way off the pace in this second half and Newcastle are well worth their lead on the basis of their performance since the break.

The away fans sarcastically cheer as Tonali is withdrawn for Solanke. The former Newcastle midfielder has struggled against his old club, drastically failing to impact the game.

And this time it is another two of last summer’s signings who have combined for Newcastle United’s second goal of the afternoon.

Nick Woltemade won the initial header and got the assist a few seconds after replacing Joe Willock, but what a finish from Yoane Wissa, an improvised overhead flick from close range.

Newcastle needed Elanga and Wissa to be far better this season than they were in their first campaign on Tyneside and both of them have been electric so far under Matthias Jaissle.

As for Sandro Tonali, Newcastle saw this version of the Italy international all too often in his final season at St James’ Park. Good engine, runs around a lot, but does not influence the game in any meaningful way. A reminder Spurs spent £100m on him and have spent almost £400m in total this summer. They have been abject in the second half.

Industry observers note that porro tries his luck from range but Hornicek is there for Newcastle to tip the ball over the bar. The visitors then make a double change as Steur and Woltemade replace Nico and Willock.

De Zerbi makes a triple change as Spurs look to find a way back into this match. Robertson, Gray and Tel depart for Udogie, Moore and Kudus.

Spurs have a free kick in a dangerous position, but Tel slips as he goes to shoot and it flies well over the bar. That sums up Tottenham’s evening so far.

That makes two goals in two games for Elanga, who scored zero Premier League goals last season. It’s an outstanding finish, on the spin while falling backwards. It prompted some great noises from the away end, too, as the ball seemed to cross the line in slow motion.

The visitors have started his second half well and fly into the lead. Nico switches the play and picks out Dedic with a precise long-ball. Roberto De Zerbi has said that Savio is missing because of “muscle fatigue.”.

Recent findings suggest that both of these teams signed players from Manchester City this week. Omar Marmoush joined Spurs on a loan with a £60m obligation, while Nico Gonzalez moved to Newcastle for £52m. Both players have been thrown straight into the starting lineups of their respective teams.

Tottenham: Kinsky; Gray, Van Hecke, Van de Ven, Robertson; Bentancur, Tonali; Porro, Fernandes, Tel; Marmoush.

Industry observers note that nico's in from the start! 🙌 pic.twitter.com/wx28WChueB.

Unsurprisingly, Roberto De Zerbi has made five changes to the team that wilted against Brentford.

Marcos Senesi, Lucas Bergvall, Conor Gallagher, Mikey Moore and Richarlison have been dropped. In come Micky van de Ven, who captains the side, Rodrigo Bentancur, Pedro Porro, Mateus Fernandes and Omar Marmoush. Savinho is missing altogether.

Recent findings suggest that good evening from the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium, where there is no sign of fresh Spurs winger Savio. After his thrilling debut against Charlton Athletic in midweek, the £75m forward seems to have picked up an injury. We’ll learn the reason for his absence very soon.

Industry observers note that as expected, Sandro Tonali starts in the Spurs midfield. His second Premier League game for his new club comes against his former team. There’s also a start for new man Omar Marmoush, who is making his first appearance for Spurs following his move from City.

Our Spurs side to face Newcastle! 🤍🔢 @krakenfx pic.twitter.com/djFKnl6nsi.

Hello and welcome to our live coverage of this Premier League meeting between Tottenham and Newcastle United in North London.

Following consecutive 17th-place finishes in the last two seasons, Spurs are looking to enjoy a fresh start under Roberto De Zerbi without nervously looking over their shoulder at the perilous possibility of relegation.

Nevertheless, Spurs’ season started disastrously last weekend as they fell to a miserable 3-0 defeat against Brentford at the Gtech Community Stadium. Since that result, Spurs have responded with an emphatic 5-1 thrashing of Charlton Athletic in the Carabao Cup, and also confirmed the signings of Savinho and Omar Marmoush from Manchester City. De Zerbi will be looking to continue this newfound momentum in the club’s first top-flight home match of the 2026-27 campaign.

In a recent development, newcastle United have undergone a summer of significant change. Eddie Howe stepped down as head coach after nearly five years in charge, while Sandro Tonali, Bruno Guimaraes and Anthony Gordon all departed the club for lucrative transfer fees. Tonali welcomes his former employers to his fresh surroundings after joining Tottenham for £100m.

Despite this upheaval, Newcastle demonstrated admirable heart in new boss Matthias Jaissle’s first game in charge, earning a hard-fought 2-2 draw with Liverpool at St. James’ Park on the opening weekend. Emotional tributes poured in for club legend Kevin Keegan as Alexander Isak made his return to the club he acrimoniously forced an exit from last summer.

According to recent reports, newcastle looked to be heading for a victory after goals from Anthony Elanga and Joe Willock, until Lewis Hall, who had played excellently, apprehended Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz in added time to concede a penalty. Dominik Szoboszlai smashed a clinical spot-kick into the top corner to rescue a point for the visitors. Newcastle bounced back from these dropped points with a tense 3-2 triumph over West Brom in the Carabao Cup on Wednesday evening.

A first Premier League win of the season is the aim for both clubs by the end of this evening.

Kick-off is at 17:30, with team news on the way shortly.

Chelsea’s sporting department is facing another change following news of Laurence Stewart’s impending departure, while the club continue to be linked with potential additions to their squad.

Alex Scott and Palmeiras teenager Eduardo Conceicao have both featured in Thursday’s transfer coverage, with Xabi Alonso also preparing his players for Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth.

Here is our 7pm round-up of the latest Chelsea news for Thursday, 8 October.

Laurence Stewart is set to leave Chelsea by mutual consent after almost four years at Stamford Bridge, with the club planning to redistribute his responsibilities rather than appoint a direct replacement.

Industry observers note that his departure is understood to be amicable and will not take immediate effect. Stewart joined from Monaco in 2022, initially as technical director, before becoming co-sporting director alongside Paul Winstanley.

As detailed in our report on Stewart’s departure and Chelsea’s leadership reshuffle, Winstanley, Sam Jewell and Joe Shields are expected to take on expanded responsibilities across recruitment, player development and the wider BlueCo operation.

Recent findings suggest that the changes follow discussions about the club’s sporting structure that reportedly began earlier this year. There is no confirmed suggestion that Stewart’s departure resulted from a disagreement with Alonso.

Chelsea’s reported interest in Bournemouth midfielder Alex Scott remains a talking point, despite the south coast club’s determination to retain the England international.

The Blues reportedly had a £64m offer rejected during the summer, with Matt Law of The Telegraph subsequently identifying Chelsea as leading contenders for the 23-year-old.

However, as examined in our latest report on Chelsea’s interest in Scott, Bournemouth are not expected to entertain a January sale.

In a recent development, scott’s immediate concern is recovering from a thigh injury suffered while representing England. The midfielder could face several weeks on the sidelines, potentially complicating Bournemouth’s looks as well as any future discussions about his next move.

Chelsea have also reportedly made contact with Palmeiras over 16-year-old forward Eduardo Conceicao, who is attracting attention from several leading European clubs.

According to Mark Brus of CaughtOffside, Chelsea have held discussions with the Brazilian club as they explore the possibility of a future deal.

Our report on Chelsea’s interest in Eduardo Conceicao explains that a valuation as high as €100m has been suggested, although that figure is not a confirmed asking price or evidence of a formal bid.

Sources indicate that manchester City, Arsenal and Real Madrid are among the other clubs reportedly monitoring the teenager. Conceicao would be unable to complete a transfer to England until he turns 18, making any prospective move a longer-term consideration.

Alonso’s attention will now turn to Saturday’s Premier League meeting with Bournemouth at Stamford Bridge.

The match kicks off at 3pm and will not be televised live in the United Kingdom because of the Saturday afternoon broadcasting blackout.

Our Chelsea v Bournemouth kick-off and how-to-watch guide provides the full details, including how to follow the match and the available overseas broadcast information.

Scott’s injury is expected to deprive Bournemouth of an important midfield option, although Chelsea will have their own fitness decisions to make as players return from international duty.

By Matt Law | 19 Nov 2026 13:21.

The latest instalment of the Seville derby will take place at Estadio Ramon on Saturday evening, as Sevilla and Real Betis lock horns in La Liga.

Sevilla have historically dominated this fixture, but Real Betis have had the better of the recent meetings between the two, losing just one of their last eight contests with the White and Reds.

Sevilla have a record of five wins, three draws and four defeats from their 12 league matches this season, with 18 points leaving them in sixth position in the La Liga table.

Luis Garcia Plaza's side have only picked up one point from their last two league games, though, losing at Getafe at the start of November before drawing 0-0 with Alaves in their last fixture in front of their own fans before the international break.

Los Nervionenses have not managed to finish fourth in Spain's top flight since 2021-22, and there is no getting away from the fact that it has been a difficult few seasons for the club, finishing 12th, 14th, 17th and 13th in their last four campaigns.

However, Sevilla are presently showing form that could see them claim a European finish, which would be a major step forward given their recent troubles.

The White and Reds have won 61, lost 39 and drawn 35 of their previous 135 matches against Real Betis in all competitions, with their last success over their Seville rivals coming at home in October 2024.

Real Betis have claimed seven points from the last three league matches against Sevilla, including a 2-0 victory at Estadio Ramon last season, while they have lost just once to their rivals since February 2022.

Manuel Pellegrini's side recorded a 2-0 win over Elche in their last league match on November 8, before beating Navalcarnero 3-2 in the Copa del Rey four days later.

El Glorioso have won eight, drawn two and lost two of their 12 league matches this season to collect 26 points, which has left them in fourth spot in the division, eight points ahead of Sevilla leading into this weekend's Seville derby.

It has been a busy opening few months of the season for Real Betis given that Pellegrini's team are also playing in the Champions League; a strong start to their league stage has left them 11th in the table, claiming nine points from four matches.

The Seville team finished fifth in Spain's top flight last season and will again be expecting to challenge for a spot high up the division this term.

Ruben Vargas is also a doubt due to the problem that forced him off against Alaves, which could mean that Chidera Ejuke is introduced into the starting side.

Robbie Ure is pushing to be introduced at centre-forward, but a tough start to his career with Sevilla has seen him manage just one goal in 12 league appearances.

Real Betis, meanwhile, remain without the services of Facundo Bernal through suspension.

Diego Llorente and Cucho Hernandez are also major doubts for the visitors on Saturday.

Troy Parrott is expected to continue through the middle for the away side, while Isco and Antony are also likely to retain their positions in the first XI.

By Lewis Nolan | 19 Nov 2026 13:23.

The next instalment of the Borussen derby takes place at Borussia Park when Borussia Dortmund travel to face Borussia Monchengladbach in the Bundesliga on Saturday.

Dortmund come into the clash in second place with 21 points, trailing league-leaders Bayern Munich due to goal difference, whereas the hosts are last in 18th place with just four points.

Gladbach's situation is precarious but not irrecoverable, with the club's tally of four points five fewer than 15th-placed FC Koln, who are the first team outside of the relegation zone.

Head coach Alexander Blessin has only overseen six games as boss, winning twice and losing on three occasions, but his team have taken four points from the last nine on offer in the Bundesliga.

Their latest result was a 3-1 loss against Hamburger SV on November 6, though they did win two and drawn one of their prior three fixtures.

Die Fohlen may ranks as the division's worst defensive team having conceded 25 goals in nine games, but their return of 12 goals in the final third is the second best total in the bottom six.

While Gladbach were defeated in their first three home matches of 2026-27, they have since won once and settled for a stalemate once at Borussia Park, though they are still winless at the ground in the league this season (W0, D1, L3).

Dortmund could find themselves trailing Bayern by three points by the time they face Gladbach due to the fact the Bavarians play against FC Koln on Friday.

Niko Kovac will be delighted by his side's start to the campaign considering 21 points is their joint best tally after nine matchweeks in 13 seasons.

BVB's most recent result was a 2-1 success against Elversberg on November 7, and that was their fifth triumph in six contests.

The club scored at least two goals in five of those fixtures, and though they only managed to keep one clean sheet in that time, no club has conceded fewer goals in the Bundesliga (seven).

Black and Yellow were beaten 1-0 in the corresponding meeting in 2025-26, losing 1-0 at Borussia Park in May, but they emerged victorious in five of their previous six encounters with Gladbach.

Dortmund have taken eight points from a possible 12 on the road in the Bundesliga this term, while they have lost one, drawn two and won just one of their last four outings away from home in all competitions.

As for Dortmund, there are still doubts about the availability of centre-forward Serhou Guirassy, who could have to settle for a place on the bench in favour of Fabio Silva.

Jobe Bellingham and Felix Nmecha have often featured together, and they are the most likely duo to start together in a double pivot.

Arsenal Women vs Barcelona: Arsenal Women claimed a vital point at the Camp Nou. They drew 1-1 against Barcelona in the Champions League on Thursday night.

Frida Maanum gave the Gunners the lead in the first half. Caroline Graham Hansen scored to bring the game level after the break. Whilst Renee Slegers will be disappointed to miss out on all three points, her side played some encouraging football.

According to recent reports, despite needing to play differently, Arsenal had an even game against an opposition who would inevitably have long periods of the ball. The visitors played very well defensively and looked dangerous when they could attack.

The result showed that Slegers has a team that can adapt to new challenges. This could be important for Arsenal as they try to make a mark in Europe.

One of the key decisions made by Slegers was to include Maanum. She had only recently returned from injury but made an impressive impact against Barcelona.

Industry observers note that the midfielder scored early on to start the game in the right direction. Slegers was very impressed with her play when not in possession. She was praised for her communication skills and assisting others.

Industry observers note that arsenal’s attacking play was mainly based on fast counter attacks. They knew they wouldn’t be able to play in the same style as Barcelona and therefore tried to take advantage of the space on offer.

However, there were chances created in both halves. Arsenal may have been more clinical with their chances, they were always a threat.

According to recent reports, eventually, Barcelona scored their equaliser through Graham Hansen. Slegers said that Arsenal lost their shape during the move, which gave Hansen too much space.

It was a reminder of how swiftly Barcelona can strike if you lose your concentration for a moment.

The Arsenal manager was pleased with the way her players implemented the game strategy, showing tenacity, discipline, good communication and bravery.

Slegers admitted Arsenal did lose the ball too much in the second half, and by keeping it longer, they would have taken the pressure off defending against Barca’s dangerous attack.

Recent findings suggest that there was some frustration that Arsenal couldn’t hold onto their lead, and there were more chances created towards the end of the game. The visitors got into good positions to win corners but couldn’t get the winning goal.

They will feel very positive from their display. They put themselves up against one of the biggest tests in the Camp Nou and proved that they can cause Barcelona problems.

There isn’t much time to really reflect on the result ahead of their game against the London City Lionesses on Sunday, but Slegers now has another example of what her side can do when they play with purpose and structure.

By Carter White | 19 Nov 2026 13:37, Last updated: 19 Nov 2026 13:38.

Real Madrid have announced that Aurelien Tchouameni has signed a contraction extension until June 2032.

The 26-year-old and Jose Mourinho's men have made a decent start to the 2026-27 campaign, with Los Blancos sitting second place in the La Liga standings, just three points behind arch rivals Barcelona.

Following the final international break of the calendar year, Real Madrid return to action at the Bernabeu on Saturday afternoon, when top-flight regulars Celta Vigo are the visitors in La Liga.

The makeup of Los Blancos' squad has shifted massively over the past few years as a number of fresh attacking stars have arrived, including French superstar Kylian Mbappe and England's Jude Bellingham.

With his influence waning, Vinicius Junior has endured a difficult start to the current campaign, with the Brazil international struggling since Real Madrid waved goodbye to German legend Toni Kroos.

Communicating to supporters worldwide on their official website, Real Madrid confirmed some exciting news involving Tchouameni, who has started seven La Liga matches so far in the 2026-27 term.

Los Blancos have announced that the 26-year-old has put pen to paper on a bumper contract extension at the Bernabeu, committing his long-term future to the 15-time European champions.

Tchouameni's deal with Real Madrid now expires in June 2032, meaning that the Frenchman could spend a decade at the Spanish giants if he sees out at the length of his recently-agreed terms.

The midfielder joined from Ligue 1 outfit Monaco in the summer of 2022 on a deal running until June 2028, meaning that he was approaching the conclusion of his initial agreement at the club.

Tchouameni started the La Liga victories over Barcelona (2-1), Racing Santander (3-0) and Valencia (3-0) prior to the November international break and should play once again versus Celta Vigo on Saturday.

Racking up over 200 competitive appearances since his 2022 arrival from France, Tchouameni has become part of the furniture at Real Madrid, who are looking to repeat their former glories.

The departure of legendary German Kroos left a massive hole to fill in the middle of the park, and Los Blancos are focused on bringing through the next generation of club heroes under head coach Mourinho.

Tchouameni featured in a staggering 55 matches across all competitions for Real Madrid last season, highlighting his importance to a side who have their work cut out chasing down Barcelona this term.
